articles.title: UK Broker GCEX Opens SpaceX, Tesla and Nvidia Perpetuals to Professionals
articles.sourceName: Financial And Business News | Finance Magnates
articles.description: GCEX began offering contracts on Amazon, Nvidia, Tesla and SpaceX to professional and institutional clients today (Thursday). The London-based digital asset and FX prime broker provides them through GC Exchange Limited, its unit authorized by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). The firm calls the product real-world asset (RWA) perpetuals. In practice they are cash-settled contracts for difference (CFDs) with no expiry date, which the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has told firms fall under EU CFD rules. On crypto exchanges, stock contracts have driven most of the growth in perpetuals on traditional assets. Equity-linked volume there more than tripled to $141 billion in June from $45 billion in May, according to TokenInsight data. Same Account as Crypto and FX CFDs Many of GCEX's institutional clients already trade FX and digital asset CFDs with it and had asked for this exposure without opening an account elsewhere, the firm said. GCEX sits on the other side of every trade. It is the second product the UK unit has opened to that client base in five weeks. In October it started quoting bitcoin and ether options over the counter to hedge funds, asset managers and family offices. "We hedge our exposure with our liquidity providers," said Lars Holst, founder and chief executive of GCEX. Clients take a position on the share price without owning the stock. They get no voting rights or dividends, and dividend and corporate action adjustments are built into the contract price instead. Positions are margined and cash-settled like the firm's other products and reported on its XplorDigital platforms. More companies will follow, Holst said, depending on what clients ask for. Both launches followed a weaker year. GC Exchange Limited reported a pre-tax loss for 2025, which it linked partly to hiring, compliance and marketing costs. Other Routes Into Stock Perpetuals Single-stock perpetuals now reach traders through crypto exchanges, retail CFD brokers and US futures markets. Each route sets its own rules on who can trade them and at what leverage. For brokers weighing the product, FM Intelligence's Ask FMIQ shows which firms post the strongest volume growth. Kraken added perpetual futures to its xStocks range in February for non-US clients in more than 110 countries, at up to 20 times leverage. SpaceX has been a common starting point. Pepperstone made it the first contract in its perpetual CFD range, while Binance and CMC Markets put it in front of retail traders on the same day. The US followed in November, when the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) allowed perpetual futures to expand from bitcoin to individual stocks. GCEX's version is a bilateral CFD for professional clients and eligible counterparties only. That keeps it outside the leverage limits the FCA sets for retail CFD traders, and outside any exchange. Even for those clients, the firm's own risk warning says prices can move rapidly and losses can exceed the margin deposited. The service is not available in all jurisdictions. Outside the UK, GCEX holds a Danish license under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) through GC Exchange A/S. Its Dubai unit, GC Exchange FZE, is licensed by the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) and serves qualified and institutional investors only. This article was written by Damian Chmiel at www.financemagnates.com.

articles.title: Gold remains caught between forced liquidations and hawkish Fed bets. What could trigger a reversal?
articles.description: Gold probed briefly below the key 3,500 level yesterday before rebounding strongly and erasing most of the weekly losses. The price action has become choppy across many markets as traders await new catalysts to pick a direction. The US holiday today doesn’t help either, as thinner liquidity could lead to random price swings. For gold, it’s a tricky situation because it keeps getting smashed lower on forced liquidations when the stock market falls and the gains are capped when the sentiment improves because the US dollar and real yields get support from the hawkish repricing. Looking ahead, gold will likely need support from a dovish repricing in interest rate expectations either from weaker data, dovish Fed commentary or an end to the Iran war. But buyers will also need to be aware that a dovish repricing from renewed stock market selloff could lead to more liquidations. GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME On the daily chart, we can see that gold(CFD contract) probed briefly below the key 3,500 level but eventually bounced back to close the day above it. The buyers will likely step in around these levels, with a defined risk below the low, to position for a rally into the downward trendline. The sellers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking lower again to pile in for a drop into the 3,100 level next. GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 4 hour chart, we have a downward trendline defining the bearish momentum. We can expect the sellers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to increase the bullish bets into the major downward trendline next. GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 1 On the 1 hour chart, we have a resistance zone around the 3,600 level that adds confluence to the trendline. Again, the sellers will likely step in around these levels, with a defined risk above the resistance, to position for a drop into the 3,100 level. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break higher to increase the bullish bets into the major downward trendline next. The red lines define the average daily range for today. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

articles.title: From Sydney to Global Markets: The Story of Axi’s Growth
articles.sourceName: Financial And Business News | Finance Magnates
articles.description: Axi, the global online trading brand, is entering its 20th year. Founded in Sydney in 2007, the company now serves more than 1.4 million traders*, employs over 500 people and operates from nine offices*, with annual trading volume of $5 trillion*. The anniversary offers an opportunity for Axi to look back at how a broker built by traders, for traders, has scaled across regions, products and regulatory environments. Built by Traders, For Traders Axi began in 2007 as AxiTrader. Their idea was practical: build the brokerage they wanted to use themselves, with clear pricing, dependable execution and responsive support. That principle still shapes the business. Decisions on products, technology and service start with the trader’s experience. The market has changed a great deal since then. Retail CFD trading volumes have exploded, growing 442% from 2020 to 2025. For a long time, retail traders were focused on forex markets, with the Bank for International Settlements reporting global forex turnover at $9.6 trillion a day in April 2025, up 28% from three years earlier. However, traders’ preferences have continued to grow and evolve with changes in market conditions and available tools. This was evident in the data from Q4 2025, which showed 74% of all retail CFD activity was accounted for by metals, up from about 42% in 2020, while currency pairs had declined to just 14%. This move to multi-asset trading means that traders now expect far more from a broker than access to a price feed. For example, commodity traders might appreciate market insights like gold price predictions. Expanding Beyond Australia Axi’s first major step abroad came in 2012, when it opened a London branch. Back-office operations followed in the Dubai, Philippines, Cyprus and Singapore. Growth continued through 2018 and 2019, with expansion in China, Germany and the Middle East and North Africa. This was soon after the company reported that client trading volume had passed $100 billion a month*. Today, Axi serves clients in more than 100 countries*. The focus is on global scale with local service, including regional teams, regional regulation and support in the languages traders use. The company has grown to employ more than 500 people across nine offices*. Local market knowledge in each office adds immense practical value, as traders in different time zones deal in different currencies under different rules. Axi became a Manchester City sponsor in 2020, and the relationship has run alongside the club’s most successful years. City have won the Champions League and eight Premier League titles in that time. Axi sees a common thread in the discipline and ambition behind those results, which echoes how it approaches trading. Rebranding for a New Stage The brokerage changed direction in the second half of 2020. AxiTrader became Axi on October 1, after almost two years of work on the new identity. Axi acquired Star Financial Systems in 2020 and launched copy trading, Axi Academy and Axi Elite. Together, these milestones point to a broker that wants to offer more than just a place to execute trades. Technology that Supports the Trading Experience Axi’s platforms today include MT4 and MT5 and the Axi App. Axi also offers a Copy Trading App** in partnership with London & Eastern LLP. In September 2023, it launched Axi Select*** and became the first established broker to offer its own funded trader account programme. Deep liquidity and proprietary tools sit behind all of it to support execution. Each product suits a different kind of trader. The Axi App combines account management and trading on mobile, while MT4 and MT5 remain the choice of many experienced traders. Copy trading lets newer traders follow the strategies of others and gives experienced traders a way to share their learnings. AxiPrime, the institutional liquidity business, applies the same attention to execution for professional counterparties. In both cases the aim is straightforward: precise tools and clear pricing. Recognition and Credibility Axi Group of Companies has won over 35 awards for pricing, execution and client service. In 2025, Finance Magnates named it Most Innovative Broker, and AxiPrime won Best Execution Broker. Global Forex Awards also named Axi Group of Companies Best Broker in MENA and Latin America, and Most Reliable Broker in Asia. Looking Ahead For Axi, the next stage is about depth rather than reach. The company has built a global footprint. The task now is to keep improving the experience within it, and to support traders who want to learn as well as trade. Education remains part of that. Axi Academy, launched in 2020, gives traders structured resources on markets and trading skills, in line with the company’s focus on accessible market insight and trader development. Transparency sits alongside it. Clear communication about costs, risks and product availability helps traders make informed decisions, and that expectation will only grow as the market does. “Almost 20 years in this industry teaches you that trust is built slowly and lost quickly.”said Julie Sharova, Global Head of Marketing of Axi. “Our growth has come from staying close to what traders ask of us: clear pricing, reliable execution and tools that help them improve. Opening in a new region is usually the easier part. Holding the same standards in every region is harder, and that is where we spend most of our time.” About Axi Axi is a global online FX and CFD broker, providing millions of clients across 100+ countries with access to financial markets through intuitive trading platforms, advanced tools, and educational resources. Its product suite includes forex, CFDs, and perpetual futures, with availability varying by region and entity. articles.title: Tokyo Shares Recover Thursday as Semiconductor Buying Lifts Nikkei
articles.description: Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Average rebounded 487 yen to close at 57,499 yen on Thursday, November 26, recovering part of the previous day's sharp losses as investors bought back semiconductor and artificial intelligence-related shares, although a narrowing of gains during afternoon trading highlighted persistent concerns over technology valuations, U.S. interest rates and the outlook for global markets. The benchmark index rose 0.86%, or 487.54 points, to 57,499.16, after plunging 1,633 points on Wednesday. The broader TOPIX index gained just 4.20 points, or 0.11%, to 3,750.40, reflecting a much less convincing recovery across the wider market. The Nikkei had climbed more than 1,200 points at one stage during morning trading, briefly exceeding 58,250 as bargain hunters returned to heavily sold technology companies. However, buying momentum weakened during the afternoon, leaving the index well below its intraday high by the close. Trading remained active, with turnover on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's Prime Market reaching approximately 6.83 trillion yen on volume of 2.24 billion shares. Market breadth was almost evenly divided, with 745 stocks advancing, 750 declining and 51 finishing unchanged, suggesting that the headline index's recovery was driven by a relatively small number of heavily weighted companies. Advantest, a leading supplier of semiconductor testing equipment, made the largest contribution to the Nikkei's advance, adding approximately 234 points to the index by itself. SoftBank Group also provided substantial support, with the two companies accounting for roughly 393 points of the benchmark's 487-point gain. The concentration of buying in a handful of technology companies illustrated the market's continuing sensitivity to developments in artificial intelligence. Shares associated with AI computing, semiconductor manufacturing and data center investment have experienced increasingly volatile trading as investors reassess the scale and profitability of capital spending by major technology companies. Tokyo Electron, Kioxia Holdings, Disco and other semiconductor-related companies attracted buying during the session, helping reverse part of Wednesday's widespread selling. However, the retreat from morning highs suggested that investors remained reluctant to commit to a sustained recovery without stronger indications of stabilization in U.S. technology shares. Wall Street provided mixed signals overnight. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 164.25 points to 50,182.95 on November 25, extending its advance for a third consecutive session, while the technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 147.74 points to 23,585.80 and the S&P 500 slipped 18.31 points to 7,182.78. The Nasdaq had fallen more than 4% during the session before recovering much of its losses, demonstrating the intensity of the debate surrounding valuations in the artificial intelligence sector. Nvidia, a bellwether for global AI investment, fell 3.9% to $149.30, while memory chip manufacturer Micron Technology declined 4.6%. Amazon also lost 3.1%, reflecting continued pressure on major technology companies as investors questioned whether their enormous spending commitments would generate sufficient future earnings. Recent volatility surrounding Anthropic, which made its stock market debut in November, has added another dimension to investor concerns. The AI developer's shares recovered 1.1% to $82.79 in Wednesday's U.S. session after falling as low as $73.85, but remained slightly below their $83 initial public offering price. The company's share price has become another indicator of investor willingness to support high valuations across the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence industry. The technology selloff has also renewed attention on SoftBank Group, whose exposure to AI investments makes its shares particularly sensitive to changes in global risk appetite. The company's movements have become an important influence on the Nikkei because of its substantial weighting in the price-weighted benchmark. Outside the technology sector, Tokyo trading showed a more uneven pattern. Nonferrous metals, petroleum and coal products, and information and communications shares advanced, while food producers, pharmaceutical companies and insurers weakened. The divergence suggested some investors were shifting funds between sectors rather than increasing their overall exposure to Japanese equities. The Japanese currency remained relatively stable despite renewed discussion of monetary tightening by the Bank of Japan. The dollar traded at approximately 159.13 to 159.20 yen at 5 p.m. on Thursday, compared with around 159.21 yen the previous evening. The yen briefly strengthened into the upper 158-yen range during morning trading as Japanese exporters sold dollars ahead of month-end settlement, but the currency subsequently weakened toward 159.20 yen. Bank of Japan Policy Board member Naoki Tamura delivered a notably hawkish assessment of monetary conditions during a speech in Kofu, Yamanashi Prefecture, arguing that Japanese interest rates should move toward a neutral level as quickly as practicable. Tamura said monetary conditions remained accommodative despite the central bank's tightening measures and indicated that increases of 0.25 percentage points every few months remained an appropriate baseline for future policy adjustments. He also warned that the central bank needed to respond promptly to signs of stronger-than-expected inflation, potentially accelerating its tightening schedule if price pressures intensified. The remarks reinforced expectations that Japan's monetary policy normalization has further to run. The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark policy rate to approximately 1.25% in September, leaving investors increasingly focused on whether another increase could follow at its December meeting. Nevertheless, the yen showed little immediate reaction to Tamura's comments, suggesting that investors had already incorporated much of the expected tightening into exchange rates. Trading was also subdued ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday, when American financial markets would be closed. In Japan's bond market, the yield on the benchmark 10-year government bond was around 2.635% during afternoon trading, as investors balanced expectations of further Bank of Japan rate increases against demand for government debt following recent volatility in global equities. Japanese government bonds initially benefited from the previous session's strength in U.S. Treasuries, but gains faded as Tokyo equities recovered. The December government bond futures contract finished unchanged at 128.24. The relationship between Japanese interest rates and equity valuations remains a central consideration for investors. Higher borrowing costs could support bank lending margins but also increase financing expenses for corporations, place pressure on real estate valuations and reduce the attractiveness of highly valued growth stocks. Attention also turned to a new U.S. trade initiative that could complicate the outlook for Japanese exporters. The administration of President Donald Trump announced proposals on November 25 for additional tariffs on imports from 14 countries and regions, including Japan, following investigations into excess manufacturing capacity and related industrial policies. The U.S. Trade Representative proposed additional duties ranging from 15% to 35% under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. However, Japanese officials have sought to ensure that any measures affecting Japan remain consistent with the existing bilateral trade agreement, which provides for a maximum effective tariff rate of 15% on covered products. The proposals have renewed uncertainty for Japanese manufacturers, particularly companies operating in automobiles, steel, industrial machinery and other export-oriented industries. Although the final scope and implementation of the duties remain uncertain, the possibility of further trade restrictions could complicate investment decisions and corporate earnings forecasts. The tariff developments come as Japan's corporate sector continues to navigate a difficult combination of elevated energy costs, rising wages, exchange-rate uncertainty and changing global supply chains. Energy prices remained another significant concern. Brent crude futures were trading around $95 a barrel during Asian trading, while U.S. crude futures stood near $84, reflecting the continuing effects of geopolitical tensions and supply concerns in the Middle East. Japan, which depends heavily on imported fossil fuels, remains particularly vulnerable to sustained increases in international energy prices. A weaker yen further amplifies the cost of imported oil and gas, increasing pressure on transportation companies, manufacturers and household budgets. The government is reportedly preparing to extend gasoline subsidies under its second supplementary budget for fiscal 2026, seeking to cushion consumers and businesses against persistently high crude oil prices. The proposed measures would maintain financial support for fuel prices while the government attempts to restrain the overall size of supplementary spending. The fiscal challenge is becoming increasingly complicated as higher interest rates raise the cost of servicing government debt, narrowing the scope for additional stimulus. Among corporate developments, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group emerged in reports concerning a major financing arrangement for U.S. cloud infrastructure provider CoreWeave. Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ were reportedly preparing to seek investors for a $4.5 billion financing package, equivalent to approximately 720 billion yen, intended to support the company's borrowing requirements. The proposed financing illustrates the expanding role of Japanese financial institutions in global artificial intelligence infrastructure investment, even as equity investors grow more cautious about the sector's valuations. Data centers, advanced computing facilities and cloud infrastructure require substantial upfront capital, creating opportunities for banks and institutional investors to provide financing beyond traditional corporate lending. However, the growing financial exposure to AI infrastructure also introduces risks. Should demand for computing capacity fall short of projections, or should technology companies reduce capital expenditure, lenders could face increased scrutiny over the profitability and creditworthiness of borrowers. In the industrial sector, IHI announced the introduction of sustainable aviation fuel for testing aircraft engines following maintenance at its Mizuho facility, reflecting efforts to reduce emissions associated with aviation services. Japan Post also moved ahead with a government-supported demonstration project intended to promote more flexible parcel delivery and collection arrangements, part of broader efforts to address labor shortages and improve logistics efficiency. Suzuki announced plans to consolidate sales subsidiaries in Saitama and Chiba prefectures from December 1, simplifying its domestic distribution structure. Such restructuring reflects a wider effort among Japanese companies to improve operational efficiency as labor costs increase and demographic pressures intensify. The domestic economic outlook remains closely connected to household purchasing power. Rising food prices, energy expenses and other living costs have continued to complicate the Bank of Japan's efforts to normalize monetary policy without undermining consumer demand. Higher nominal wages have provided some support to household incomes, but persistent inflation has limited improvements in real purchasing power, leaving consumer-facing companies sensitive to changes in spending patterns. The latest U.S. inflation figures have also complicated the international interest-rate outlook. The American personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.8% from a year earlier in October, while the core measure excluding food and energy increased 3.3%, exceeding market expectations of 3.2%. The figures reinforced concerns that U.S. inflation remains sufficiently persistent to constrain the Federal Reserve's flexibility. Investors are weighing the possibility of additional monetary tightening against signs of strain in technology stocks and broader financial markets. For Japan, the combination presents a difficult policy environment. Continued U.S. monetary restraint could sustain pressure on the yen, while further Bank of Japan rate increases could raise domestic financing costs even as policymakers seek to support economic growth. The immediate market calendar will place renewed emphasis on Japan's November inflation data, including Tokyo consumer prices, which are expected to provide additional evidence of whether underlying price pressures remain strong enough to justify further monetary tightening. Investors will also monitor industrial production, retail sales and labor-market indicators for signs of how manufacturers and households are responding to higher costs and softer global demand. With U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving on November 26, Tokyo trading is likely to remain particularly sensitive to domestic economic announcements, currency movements and changes in semiconductor-sector sentiment when regular American trading resumes. Thursday's recovery offered some relief following Wednesday's steep decline, but the limited advance in the broader TOPIX index and the concentration of gains in a few technology stocks demonstrated that confidence in a sustained market rebound has yet to return. The Nikkei remains vulnerable to further swings in AI-related valuations, while the yen's proximity to 160 per dollar, the Bank of Japan's tightening plans and the renewed threat of U.S. tariffs have created additional uncertainty for Japanese businesses entering the final weeks of the year. (News On Japan)

articles.title: Gold & Silver Rebound on MCX Nov 26, 2026: Check City-Wise Rates
articles.description: After sharp swings in recent sessions, gold and silver futures staged a strong intraday rebound on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) on Thursday, November 26, 2026, supported by value buying at lower levels even as global bullion cues remained mixed. On the MCX, the December 4, 2026 gold futures contract opened ₹1,603 (1.32%) higher at ₹1,22,740 per 10 grams against its previous close of ₹1,21,137, surged to an intraday peak of ₹1,23,888 (up ₹2,751 or 2.27%), and traded around ₹1,22,549 to ₹1,22,790 per 10 grams in afternoon deals. Similarly, February 2027 gold futures climbed ₹1,568 (1.27%) to ₹1,25,003 per 10 grams across a turnover of 9,243 lots, while December 4, 2026 silver futures opened at ₹1,45,800 per kg (up ₹3,282 or 2.30% from the previous close of ₹1,42,517), touched an intraday high of ₹1,48,801 (up ₹6,284 or 4.40%), and traded near ₹1,45,465 to ₹1,47,613 per kg. Across international markets, COMEX gold futures gained roughly 0.79% to around $3,563.8 per troy ounce amid thin US Thanksgiving holiday volumes, whereas spot gold hovered near $3,571.79 to $3,578.72 per ounce (down roughly 0.1% to 0.96% after recovering from overnight dips below $3,500) as stronger US PCE inflation data (3.8%) reinforced expectations of a potential 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December. For retail jewellery buyers, wedding shoppers, and bullion investors across Uttar Pradesh—including households and sarafa markets in Lucknow and neighboring commercial hubs such as Unnao, Kanpur, Prayagraj, and Varanasi, where late-November wedding season demand keeps physical bullion counters active—tracking both MCX volatility and city-wise retail rates is essential before making purchases. MCX Futures & International Bullion Snapshot (November 26, 2026) Commodity / Benchmark Contract Opening / Reference Rate Intraday High / Spot Level Key Market Movement MCX Gold (Dec 4, 2026 Expiry) Opened at ₹1,22,740 / 10g (Prev. close ₹1,21,137) Touched ₹1,23,888 / 10g (+2.27%) Traded around ₹1,22,549–₹1,22,790 / 10g on fresh lower-level buying. MCX Gold (Feb 2027 Expiry) Up ₹1,568 (+1.27%) Traded at ₹1,25,003 / 10g Active participation with 9,243 lots traded on MCX. MCX Silver (Dec 4, 2026 Expiry) Opened at ₹1,45,800 / kg (Prev. close ₹1,42,517) Touched ₹1,48,801 / kg (+4.40%) Outperformed gold in percentage gains, trading around ₹1,45,465–₹1,47,613 / kg. International COMEX & Spot Gold COMEX gold up 0.79% to ~$3,563.8 / oz Spot gold around $3,571.79–$3,578.72 / oz Mixed global cues amid US Thanksgiving thin trade and US Fed rate-hike expectations. City-Wise Retail Gold and Silver Rates Across Major Indian Cities In physical bullion markets, retail quotes for 24-carat gold, 22-carat jewellery gold, and 1 kg fine silver reflect local taxes, transport costs, and jeweller premiums (excluding 3% GST and making charges): City 24-Carat Gold (per 10g) 22-Carat Gold (per 10g) Silver Rate (per 1 kg) New Delhi ₹1,26,040 ₹1,15,550 ₹1,65,000 Lucknow Mumbai ₹1,25,890 ₹1,15,400 Kolkata Chennai What Market Experts Suggest for Investors Amid Bullion Volatility Despite Thursday's sharp bounce on the MCX, market analysts caution retail investors and traders against committing large lump sums immediately after steep corrections. Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus, advised investors not to rush into aggressively averaging down after sharp declines, noting that staggered buying and disciplined position sizing remain far more sensible strategies because a durable uptrend requires sustained institutional and physical buying interest rather than a single-session relief rally. Similarly, wealth strategists emphasize treating gold and silver as long-term portfolio diversifiers—allocating gradually via sovereign/digital gold, ETFs, or staggered physical purchases—rather than chasing intraday futures swings.
